entries.reason: Add-participant combines search, selection, and encounter mutation glue until workflow growth justifies a split.
Encounter detail coordinates combat, map, and participant panels while capped before more orchestration accumulates.
Notes panel owns the note list, editor state, and campaign mutations until list/editor concerns split clearly.
Monster tab is the NPC-side view over monster reference data and related actions.
NPC panel coordinates list and selected-detail state while future workflows split list helpers out.
The homebrew entry dialog owns shared editor chrome for several entry kinds while repeated form sections settle.
Magic item form fields are a dense schema-aligned surface pending obvious field-group extraction.
Monster form data centralizes defaults and parse/serialize helpers without absorbing UI logic.
Monster form fields mirror a large SRD/homebrew shape while the grouped form remains intact.
The stats-tab roll panel is one compact VTT surface, with further roll modes expected to extract components.
Settings is a page-level account/preferences surface capped until another settings area is added.
Map canvas state is centralized around one store boundary while future map workflows move to helper slices.
Encounter fixtures keep related test data in one canonical scenario module for client tests.
SRD fixtures are cross-cutting reference data for client tests until another fixture family appears.
The tRPC mock is the shared client test harness for provider setup and mock procedure plumbing.
Encounter routing is still the main orchestration surface for combat and map workflows until split behind services.
Homebrew routing carries several entry-type workflows while shared entry helpers are factored out.

SRD routing is one cohesive read-only boundary for canonical reference queries and their Prisma-to-schema mapping; keeping those closely related list/get seams together preserves a discoverable reference-query surface while the cap bounds routine endpoint edits.

Rest behavior remains a tightly related transaction boundary for short- and long-rest state transitions, persistence checks, and post-commit broadcasts pending a service split; the exception can be lowered or removed when those flows move into focused services.
Rules-domain calculator has several tightly-coupled D&D damage branches pending a future rules refactor.
The SRD weapon catalog remains a reviewable transcribed rules table beside its closed property and value types.
Lcov parser holds record dispatch and note construction together; duplicate-record disclosure pushed it just over the floor until value parsing splits out.
Comparison, ranking, and finding construction share this module; config validation pushed it just over the floor until ranking splits out.

Single validator entrypoint covering every harness surface (lint rules, ratchets, hook wiring, verify steps, lint guidance, restricted-disable rules, config surfaces, smoke subjects); the 2026-07 lint deep-dive extended several of these families at once.

Verify-step generator, the marker-bridge superset guard that keeps pre-commit's slots in lockstep with the verify/verify:changed markers, and the VERIFY_STEP_PROJECTIONS descriptor naming every output this generator writes and which harness:check surface re-renders it. Do not split the descriptor into a sibling module: it must import renderVerifyStepsShellFromManifest, which needs this file's private consumer/slot helpers, so the sibling re-imports its parent and `lint:import-cycles --fail-on-runtime-cycles` fails the gate (measured 2026-08-16: the split is otherwise green, 385 effective lines). Splitting the renderer cluster out instead is the open option.

Hook wiring schema is the cohesive owner of platform event, matcher, output-capability, canonical adapter-surface projection, and manifest parsing/validation contracts; Markdown projection lives in hook-wiring-doc.ts. The projection tables cannot move to a sibling module without widening the harness-check fixture copy closure this file already sits in.
The ratchet registry grows as new ratchets land; the floor protects against accidental drift, not registry growth.
